description: Landscape comparison of real VACE and FaithfulFaces frames from Figure 13. The same restrained 3% camera push applies to both source images and continues after the divider finishes. Images remain published static outputs, not synthesized moving faces or bodies.
pairing_evidence: Figure 13, PDF page 21 (append_vis_case_2-cropped.png in arXiv HTML): one shared reference face and prompt describe a person wearing headphones and a black outfit, dancing in a park with arms raised. Comparison uses the third displayed column in the VACE and FaithfulFaces rows. Source methods generate separate outputs, so this is a same-condition comparison, not pixel-aligned or synchronous-video footage.
design_rationale: Retain the accepted landscape comparison and clean sweep. A 3.25-second divider reveal is followed by 3.1 seconds of the result, while one continuous 3% camera push runs across the whole clip at constant logarithmic speed. The matched camera transform preserves a fair comparison and avoids integer-crop jitter. No top title, slideshow, artificial blur, retouching or invented baseline.
poster_selection: Figure 13 FaithfulFaces row, fourth column, xref1308: graceful side pose with natural partly open eyes, full head, upper body and park surroundings. Different from the earlier tight vertical headphones portrait. Poster has no baked-in text; webpage typography is separate.
image_processing: Original PDF embedded pixels extracted without retouching. Both images receive the same centered floating-bound crop and Lanczos scale from 1.00 to 1.03 over seven seconds. The accepted fourth-column poster retains its original unzoomed crop and exact output bytes.
rebuild: python3 scripts/build_faithful_motion.py --source-dir /path/to/cache; missing PDF and embedded assets are downloaded/extracted and verified.

camera_motion.curve: constant logarithmic scale speed over the full 7 seconds

video_source_audit.finding: The public gallery provides no Figure 13 video. Figure 15 is a different reference identity and urban setting, so it is not a valid replacement for the Figure 13 park comparison. The current edit retains the authenticated static pair and introduces camera motion only.
